llamacppCatalog.description: Top-tier code generation and FIM. Recommended for serious coding work on 24GB+ VRAM cards.
Excellent code model for mid-tier hardware. Strong FIM, fast on 16GB cards.
Solid code model for 8GB cards. Best small-tier option for FIM.
Compact code model for low-VRAM machines. Lower quality than 7B but viable for FIM autocomplete.
Mixture-of-experts: 30B params, 3B active. Fast inference at 30B-quality. Strong reasoning + tools.

Qwen3.6 27B MTP-variant GGUF — contains NextN/MTP speculative-decode layers. When Performance Mode is on, llama-server uses --spec-type draft-mtp for 1.4×+ tok/s on high-VRAM GPUs. Requires a 20GB+ VRAM card; tested live at 110 tok/s (RTX 5090) vs 75 tok/s without (beta.25 A3 2026-06-02).
General-purpose 14B with strong reasoning and tool calling. Great for chat + agentic loop.
Solid 8B for everyday chat + tools. Runs comfortably on 8GB cards.
Meta's flagship open model. State-of-the-art quality at 70B; needs 48GB+ VRAM at usable quants.
Reliable 8B chat model. Strong tool-calling support, well-tested.
Microsoft's compact reasoning model. Strong on code + math, MIT license.
llamacppCatalog._toolsNote: ModelProfileService pins phi-4-14b to nativeFunctionCalling=false. Catalog matches profile reality so the agentic loop and llama-server flag (--jinja) stay consistent.

llamacppCatalog.description: Google's open model, strong general-purpose chat with multilingual coverage.
llamacppCatalog._toolsNote: Gemma family pinned to nativeFunctionCalling=false in ModelProfileService — Joe-tested 2026-05-05, Gemma 4 degenerated into thinking-only output after 3-4 successful tool calls. Same defensive posture for Gemma 3.

llamacppCatalog.description: Apache 2.0, fast 24B. Strong coding + chat balance.
Mistral's updated Small 3.2 (2506) — better instruction-following and fewer repetition loops than 3.1. Apache 2.0, strong coding + chat balance for 16GB+ cards.
Mistral's coding-focused 24B with native FIM tokens. Excellent for autocomplete + agentic edits.
Reasoning-tuned distill of Qwen 14B. Strong on math + multi-step problems. Slower due to think tokens.
Tiny but capable. Great for low-VRAM laptops or fast chat on bigger machines.
Tiny FIM model — fast autocomplete on integrated graphics or low-VRAM laptops. Also usable as a speculative-decoding draft model for the Qwen2.5-Coder family (7B/14B/32B targets).
Compact general chat model. Fits on integrated graphics. Good baseline for low-end hardware.
HuggingFace's SmolLM3 3B — a current-gen small model with dual-mode reasoning and tool calling. Runs on very low VRAM; a strong pick for laptops and integrated graphics.
Vision-language model based on Mistral 7B. Captures + describes images, reads UI screenshots, identifies text and elements. Pairs with the Preview tab so the agent can see what it's editing.
1.8B vision model — fast, low VRAM. Good for quick visual descriptions and rough OCR. Use this on small GPUs or when latency matters more than vision quality.

Qwen's 7B vision-language model — strong OCR, document and screenshot understanding, and chart/diagram reading. Higher visual quality than LLaVA 1.6 at a similar size; the best general-purpose VLM in the catalog for reading UI and text in images.

Qwen3's 8B vision-language model — the current-generation successor to Qwen2.5-VL. Strong OCR, document/screenshot understanding, and chart reading. The best general-purpose VLM in the catalog for reading UI and text in images.
Google's Gemma 4 E4B — a compact, natively multimodal model (text + vision) that runs on small GPUs. Reads screenshots, documents, and charts.
llamacppCatalog._toolsNote: Gemma family is pinned to nativeFunctionCalling=false in ModelProfileService (json-fenced format) — supportsTools:false here matches that. Gemma degenerates into thinking-only output after a few native tool calls (Joe-tested, same as gemma-3-27b).

llamacppCatalog.description: Qwen3's flagship open code model — mixture-of-experts (30B total, 3B active) for fast, high-quality code generation, FIM, and agentic edits. The current top local coding pick for 24GB+ cards.
Google's Gemma 4 12B — a natively multimodal model (text + vision) with strong general chat plus screenshot, document, and chart reading. A capable mid-size VLM for 12GB+ cards.
llamacppCatalog._toolsNote: Gemma family is pinned to nativeFunctionCalling=false in ModelProfileService — supportsTools:false matches that. Gemma degenerates into thinking-only output after a few native tool calls (Joe-tested, same as gemma-3-27b / gemma-4-e4b).

llamacppCatalog.description: DeepSeek's R1-0528 reasoning distilled into Qwen3-8B — SOTA chain-of-thought quality at 8B, runs on 8GB cards. Slower output due to think tokens. Stronger than the older R1 Qwen distills at the same size.
Qwen3.5 9B — a strong current-generation general chat + tool-calling model that runs comfortably on 8GB cards. A good all-round default for mid-tier hardware.
Qwen3's large vision-language MoE (30B total, 3B active) — the highest-quality VLM in the catalog for OCR, document/screenshot understanding, and chart/diagram reading. For 24GB+ cards.

Qwen3's 32B dense vision-language model — the highest-quality dense VLM in the catalog for OCR, document/screenshot understanding, and chart/diagram reading. For 24GB+ cards. (Qwen3-VL has no 7B dense variant; the 8B entry above is the small-tier pick.)

OpenBMB's MiniCPM-V 4.5 — an efficient 8B vision-language model with strong OCR and high-resolution image / document understanding. Runs on 8GB+ cards. Needs a recent llama.cpp build with MiniCPM-V support.

Qwen 3 1.7B — the same tokenizer + chat template as Qwen3-8B/14B/30B, making it ideal as a speculative-decoding draft model for those targets. Unlocks 1.3–1.5× throughput on Qwen3 chat + code models with no quality loss. Downloadable once chunk 1b draft-flag wiring ships.

Meta's Llama 3.2 1B — shares the Llama 3 tokenizer with Llama 3.1-8B, Llama 3.3-70B, Mistral Small 24B, and Devstral 24B, making it a natural draft companion for all those targets. Downloadable once chunk 1b draft-flag wiring ships.

Qwen's next-generation 80B code MoE — the flagship local coder for 48GB+ VRAM cards. Ships as a 4-shard GGUF; Bodega downloads all shards and loads them as one model. Q4_K_M is ~45 GB across four files.
DeepSeek's next flagship MoE (~172GB total weight). Cloud-only via the DeepSeek API preset — no mainstream-llama.cpp GGUF available at this size.
